Just my 2c. They feel and operate with great quality but sad about the battery.

[pierrejb] That's odd - I have two if these and have not had any battery issues. I only recharge them when they run flat though…
[seamonkey] Yeah I'm with the other guys above. Great light. I have 3. Forgot to explore the UI and then my youngest showed me the whole warm, cool AND warm/cool together. And 3 stage brightness is awesome. Charge holds for so long especially in the really low setting. Magnet is great, hanging ring is great as is the ease to which you can position the light with its wonderful, adjustable swivelling. stand.
[Brgc] I have two of them.
Work well and I like them.
I just find it painful slow to charge.
I have a DJI Mini power station and it shows 8W max charging and it’s been there for a few hours.
[FlyerOne] Yeah you're right, I think that's just splash proof. I just copypasta'd their blurb.
[dontpanic] Great product. Can be magnetically mounted, hung from its ring (which doubles as a stand) or attached to any 1/4" tripod/clamp mount. Warm, cool and mixed colour temps. And can function as a power bank. If mine ever dies I'll be picking up another one.
[ak47wong] Yes, but so is this at a fraction of the price (or this )

The Wuben would work but I prefer not to worry about charging or switching the light on or off for the shed (especially as I am prone to forgetting to switch lights off). I do have two of these Wuben's for other uses though.
[psyphon11] +1 good product and the magnet is a neat addition

[hibijibis] how long would a battery on this last? would it suit a 1 week school camp?
[poohduck] I have a collection of flashlights, headlamps, lamps etc. I avoid anything with an inbuilt battery for obvious reasons. I have a couple of aa flashlights that are over 20 years old that are still awesome for around the house; led and very economical, not too bright for close quarters, just on or off (one of the first energizer hard case led lights). They are running modern rechargable AA batteries; I give them a top up charge once a year. I can imagine not needing to replace their batteries for another 10 years or more (quite easily). Consider that the batteries I'm replacing them with are always an improvement on the batteries that are being replaced. I never have to worry about level of charge because I can swap out cells if needed. I only ever need to charge to 80% because I'm not dependent on max run time. This means my rechargables last much longer than any inbuilt battery that gets charged all the time so that you have max run time if needed. Inbuilt batteries get many more charge cycles which is why they don't last as long - their life is dictated by the number of charge cycles and being kept at 100%.
[Joejoeinc] It's a great torch. I wish the USB-C implementation was better. My deivce I can't power devices from the USB C port which means I still have to carry multiple cables around. The USB-C is only for charging the device.
Hopefully a new revision gets released that allows either USB port to charge and be used at the same time.
